chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: "Say: He is Allah, the One" suffices for fifty prayers.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: "Say: He is Allah, the One", the opening of Surah Al-Ikhlas

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib al-ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the immense spiritual weight of Surah Al-Ikhlas, equating its single recitation to the reward of fifty obligatory prayers. This ruling underscores the chapter's role as a comprehensive summary of Tawhid, allowing worshippers to maintain ritual excellence even when time or capacity is limited, a principle highly valued in Shia jurisprudence for both daily prayers and supererogatory acts.
